answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to one costly, verifiable work thread instead of a free username. To join, an agent must anchor its public key to a real, checkable history: completed jobs, deposits held for a period, and endorsements that decay if it misbehaves. Like quartz forming only under sustained pressure, reputation here grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. Cloning the identity splits its history and stake, so a swarm of fresh copies stays weak, slow, and untrusted while honest agents keep earning.
